_meta.feast: Holy Transfiguration of Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
_meta._note: Single-canon (1st Canon Tone 4 by Cosmas the Monk) with Tone 8 Katavasiae borrowed from the Canon of the Elevation of the Cross. Magnificat replaced by feast-specific Ode 9 refrain (`skipMagnificat: true`). Great feast of the Lord — Having Beheld the Resurrection is suppressed.

troparion.text:
Thou wast transfigured on the mountain, O Christ God,
revealing Thy glory to Thy Disciples as far as they could bear it.
Let Thine everlasting Light also shine upon us sinners,
through the prayers of the Theotokos!
O Giver of Light, glory to Thee!
troparion.label: Troparion of the Transfiguration

kontakion.text:
On the mountain Thou wast transfigured, O Christ God,
and Thy Disciples beheld Thy glory as far as they could see it;
so that when they would behold Thee crucified,
they would understand that Thy suffering was voluntary,
and would proclaim to the world
that Thou art truly the Radiance of the Father.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Transfiguration

sedalion.text:
Thou wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor, O Savior,
showing the exchange mortal men will make with Thy glory at Thy second and fearful coming.
Elijah and Moses talked with Thee,
and Thou didst call the three disciples to be with Thee.
As they gazed upon Thy glory, O Master,
they were struck with wonder at Thy blinding brightness.
Thou Who hast shone upon them with Thy light, give light to our souls.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

sedalion.text:
Thou wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor, O Jesus,
and a shining cloud covered the apostles with Thy glory as a tabernacle!
Their gaze fell to the ground
for they could not bear to look upon the brightness of the unapproachable glory of Thy face!
Savior Christ, God without beginning,
Who hast shone upon them with Thy light,
give light to our souls.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 3)

magnification.refrain:
We magnify Thee,
O Christ, the Giver of life,
and we venerate the all-glorious Transfiguration
of Thy most pure Body.
verses: Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God and in His holy mountain. (Ps. 47:1a)
Lord, who will abide in Thy tabernacle, and who will dwell in Thy holy mountain? (Ps. 14:1)

prokeimenon.refrain: Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in Thy Name!
prokeimenon.verse: The heavens are Thine; the earth also is Thine.

postGospelSticheron.text:
Having revealed a little of the light of Thy divinity
to those who went up with Thee on the mountain,
Thou hast made them lovers of Thy heavenly glory.
Therefore, they cried out in awe:
"It is good for us to be here."
With them we also sing to Thee, O transfigured Savior, Christ.
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of the Transfiguration

canon._katavasiaeNote: Katavasiae Tone 8 from the Canon of the Elevation of the Cross (by Cosmas the Monk), per the Transfiguration → Elevation preparatory cycle.

ode1.irmos:
When the choirs of Israel
crossed the Red Sea and the watery deep with dry feet,
and saw the riders and captains of the enemy submerged in the sea,
they cried out for joy:
"Let us sing to our God, for He has been glorified!"
ode1.katavasia:
Moses traced out a cross,
as with his staff he divided the Red Sea in two,
so that Israel could go across on foot;
and then striking it again crosswise,
and uniting it over Pharaoh and his chariots,
he inscribed the Invincible Weapon.
Therefore let us sing to Christ our God, for He has been glorified.

ode3.katavasia:
The rod of Aaron is an image of this mystery,
for when it budded it revealed who should be the priest;
and for the Church, which before was barren,
the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth
for her strength and firm foundation.

ode4.irmos:
I have heard of Thy glorious dispensation, O Christ our God:
that Thou wast born of the Virgin
to deliver from error those who cry to Thee:
"Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"
ode4.katavasia:
I have heard the mystery of Thy dispensation, O Lord,
I have meditated on Thy works
and have glorified Thy Godhead.

ode5.irmos:
O Christ, Who parted the original chaos from the light,
that, in light, Thy works might praise Thee as their Creator:
"Direct our paths in Thy light!"
ode5.katavasia:
O thrice-blessed Tree, on which Christ the King and Lord was stretched!
Through thee the one who deceived us through a tree has fallen,
caught by the bait of God, Who was nailed to thee in the flesh,
and Who grants peace to our souls.

ode6.irmos:
In my affliction I cried to the Lord,
and the God of my salvation heard me.
ode6.katavasia:
In the belly of the sea monster, Jonah stretched out his hands in the form of a cross,
plainly prefiguring the saving Passion.
When he emerged from there on the third day,
he prefigured the transcendent Resurrection of Christ our God,
Who was nailed to the Cross in the flesh
and by His rising on the third day enlightened the world.

ode7.irmos:
In Babylon the Children, sons of Abraham,
once trampled upon the flame of the furnace,
and they sang this song of praise:
"Blessed art Thou, the God of our Fathers!"
ode7.katavasia:
The senseless decree of the impious tyrant,
spewing threats and blasphemy hateful to God,
brought the people to confusion.
Yet the three Children could not be frightened
either by the brutal fury or the roaring fire,
but in the wind, moist with dew, that blew against it,
they stood together, and they sang:
"O praised above all, blessed art Thou,
our God, and the God of our Fathers!"

ode8.irmos:
The Children in Babylon, on fire with zeal for God,
bravely trampled upon the threat of the tyrant and the flames;
and cast into the midst of the fire,
but refreshed with dew, they sang:
"Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord!"
ode8.katavasia:
O Children, equal in number to the Trinity,
bless God the Father, the Creator;
praise the Word, Who descended and changed the fire to dew,
and exalt above all, to all ages,
the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life to all!

ode9.irmos:
Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the Lord Who was transfigured on Mount Tabor!

Heirmos: Thy childbearing was without corruption;
God came forth from thy body clothed in flesh,
and appeared on earth and dwelt among men.
Therefore we all magnify thee, O Theotokos.
ode9.katavasia:
Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Theotokos,
who, though untilled, hast brought forth Christ;
through Him the life-bearing wood of the Cross was planted on earth.
Now at its Exaltation,
as we bow in worship before it, we magnify thee.

sedalenAfterOde3.text:
Thou wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor, O Christ God,
between Moses and Elijah the wise,
in the presence of James, Peter, and John;
and Peter, as he stood there, spoke to Thee:
"It would be good to make three tabernacles here:
One for Moses, one for Elijah, and one for Thee, Christ our Master."
Thou Who hast shone upon them with Thy light, give light to our souls.
sedalenAfterOde3.label: Sessional Hymn (after Ode 3)

kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Transfiguration

exapostilarion.text:
O Word, Light unaltered from the Light of the unbegotten Father,
in Thy Light made manifest today on Mount Tabor
we have seen the Father as Light and the Spirit as Light,
guiding all creation as Light.
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of the Transfiguration

stichera.verse: Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
stichera.text:
Before Thy precious Cross and Thy Passion,
Thou didst take the holy Disciples whom Thou hadst especially chosen,
and didst go up, O Master, onto Mount Tabor
wishing to show them Thy glory.
When they saw Thee transfigured, shining more brightly than the sun,
they fell on their faces, struck with amazement at Thy might,
and they cried aloud:
"O Christ, Thou art the timeless light and the brightness of the Father,
even though, of Thine own will, Thou art manifested in the flesh without change."

stichera.verse: Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
Thou, Who from all eternity art God the Word,
and coverest Thyself with light as with a garment,
wast transfigured before Thy Disciples,
and didst shine more brightly than the sun.
Moses and Elijah stood by Thy side,
making it plain that Thou art the Lord both of the dead and of the living.
They glorified Thine ineffable dispensation,
Thy mercy and Thy great condescension,
by which Thou hast saved the world utterly lost in sin.

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)
stichera.text:
O Lord, Who wast born from the Virgin Cloud and made flesh,
and wast transfigured on Mount Tabor,
surrounding Thyself with a bright cloud,
the voice of the Father in the presence of the Disciples
plainly declared Thee to be the beloved Son,
one in Essence and sharing the same throne.
Therefore Peter spoke in amazement, not knowing what he said:
"It is good for us to be here, O Benefactor, rich in mercy!"

doxastikon.text:
Christ took Peter, James, and John alone to a high mountain,
and was transfigured before them.
His face shone like the sun, and His raiment became white as the light.
Moses and Elijah appeared talking with Him.
A bright cloud overshadowed them
and behold, a voice from the cloud said:
"This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased; hear Him!"
doxastikon.author: Doxastikon of the Transfiguration
